record.paper_title: Open problems of the 32nd Workshop on Cycles and Colourings
record.original_question: Is χ⋆ℓ(G) ≤ 7 for every planar graph G, where χ⋆ℓ(G) is the least k such that every k-list-assignment of G admits k pairwise disjoint proper L-colorings?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.7 Is it true that χ⋆ ℓ(G)≤7 for every planar graph?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G = (V, E) be a finite simple graph. A list assignment for G is a function L that assigns to every vertex v ∈ V a finite set L(v) of colors; if |L(v)| = k for every v ∈ V, then L is called a k-list-assignment. A proper L-coloring of G is a function c : V → ⋃_{v∈V} L(v) such that c(v) ∈ L(v) for every v ∈ V and c(u) ≠ c(v) whenever uv ∈ E. Two L-colorings c₁ and c₂ are said to be disjoint if c₁(v) ≠ c₂(v) for every v ∈ V. The list packing number χ⋆_ℓ(G) is defined as the least positive integer k such that for every k-list-assignment L of G there exist k pairwise disjoint proper L-colorings of G.

Prove or disprove: for every planar graph G, χ⋆_ℓ(G) ≤ 7.
artifact.status_search_result: The best known upper bound for the list packing number of an arbitrary planar graph is χ⋆_ℓ(G) ≤ 8, established by Cambie, Cames van Batenburg, Davies and Kang and refined in subsequent work on list and correspondence packing of planar graphs. No proof (or counterexample) of the bound 7 appears in the literature, so the problem is open.

status_evidence.title: List Packing and Correspondence Packing of Planar Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: χ*_ℓ(G) ≤ 8 for planar graphs with girth at least 3; ≤ 5 for girth ≥ 4; ≤ 4 for girth ≥ 5.
status_evidence.claim: The current best general upper bound for planar graphs is 8, not 7.

status_evidence.title: Fractional List Packing for Layered Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses fractional list packing and related conjectures for planar graphs.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work continues to investigate list packing numbers of planar graphs without establishing the bound 7.
